We have identified a profound mispricing in the Company, where technical demand from a retail-driven short squeeze has decoupled the shares from any rational assessment of intrinsic value [D01][D07]. The current market capitalization of approximately $8.01 billion is an anomaly that ignores the company’s severe fundamental distress [D04][D05].

Our sum-of-the-parts analysis, factoring in the company’s heavy leverage, significant operating losses, and the structural pressures on its business segments, suggests an equity value in the range of $2.00 to $5.00 per share [D01][D04][D05]. In contrast, operators like Cinemark and IMAX maintain superior margins, demonstrating the competitive disadvantage and secular challenges facing the Company’s core assets [D06].

Market participants are currently ignoring the reality that this is a zero-sum game, where the company’s high debt seniority and the ongoing dilution from at-the-market equity programs threaten to leave common shareholders with no recovery [D01][D03][D05]. With over $900 million raised or committed to alleviate near-term liquidity concerns, the company is effectively diluting its way to survival rather than creating value [D01][D02][D03].

Our role is purely opportunistic; we are positioning to capitalize on this price dislocation as the technical squeeze eventually exhausts [D01]. We have no interest in engaging with a management team presiding over such a distressed capital structure [D04].

Risks to our thesis include the irrational persistence of retail-driven momentum and the potential for further dilutive financing that could sustain the stock price in the near term [D01][D05][D07]. We are sizing this position at 1% of NAV to account for the extreme volatility associated with gamma squeezes and the difficulty of predicting the timing of technical exhaustion [D05][D07].
